# Code Review Report — PR #240
**Branch:** feat/issue-230-migrate-reviewer-family
**Reviewer:** Qwen (Reviewer mode)
**Date:** 2026-04-29

## Review Summary

This PR migrates the reviewer family into `.opencode/agents/` and updates the OpenCode orchestrator to use the filename-derived reviewer names. The landed diff resolves the earlier hard mismatch between parenthetical reviewer names and the new filenames; I did not find a remaining correctness or security defect in the changed files themselves.

The main remaining risk is verification coverage. This migration depends on OpenCode resolving `reviewer-kimi.md`, `reviewer-qwen.md`, `reviewer-glm.md`, and `pr-reviewer.md` to the exact task names now referenced by the orchestrator, but the PR does not include any smoke-test evidence that those dispatches were exercised successfully.

**Files Reviewed:** 6
**Findings:** 0 Critical, 1 Warning, 1 Suggestion

## Findings

### Critical Findings

None.

### Warning Findings

```text
[W-01] Reviewer-family dispatch rename is still unverified at runtime
Category: Testing
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/orchestrator-v3.md
Lines: 38-45, 69, 550-555
Description: The orchestrator now relies on OpenCode deriving task-dispatch names
from filenames such that `reviewer-kimi.md` maps to "Reviewer Kimi",
`reviewer-qwen.md` maps to "Reviewer Qwen", `reviewer-glm.md` maps to
"Reviewer Glm", and `pr-reviewer.md` maps to "Pr Reviewer". That assumption is
plausible and consistent with the existing `test-writer.md` → "Test Writer"
pattern documented in the repository's migration plan, but this PR contains no
verification artifact, test, or recorded smoke run proving the exact dispatch
names work in practice. Because these changes are pure runtime configuration, a
name-resolution mismatch would only surface when Step 7 or `@pr-reviewer` is
actually invoked, and it would break the review workflow without any automated
check catching it.
Suggestion: Before merge, run one end-to-end Step 7 synthesized local review and
one manual `@pr-reviewer` invocation against a draft PR, then record the result
in the PR description or a review note. If this migration pattern will recur,
add a lightweight validation check that asserts the expected agent names are
dispatchable under OpenCode.
```

### Suggestions

```text
[S-01] PR reviewer naming remains split across slug, derived task name, and prose
Category: Documentation
Severity: Suggestion
File: .opencode/agents/pr-reviewer.md
Lines: 1-30, 103
Description: The file is manually invoked as `@pr-reviewer`, the orchestrator now
allow-lists `Pr Reviewer`, and the body/report template still refer to the agent
as "PR Reviewer". This does not appear to break execution by itself, but it does
leave three naming surfaces for the same agent. That makes debugging dispatch
problems harder, especially because this PR's core behavior depends on
filename-derived naming.
Suggestion: Add one explicit note near the top of the file stating the manual
invocation form (`@pr-reviewer`) and, if relevant, the derived OpenCode task name
used by orchestrator dispatch. Alternatively, normalize the prose to the same
display name used in `.opencode/agents/orchestrator-v3.md`.
```

## Overall Assessment

The migration is close and the important structural fix is present: the orchestrator now references the filename-derived reviewer names consistently in both the `permission.task.allow` list and the Step 7 dispatch order. I found no blocking correctness, security, or documentation defect in the changed files themselves after that fix.

I would still hold merge until the runtime naming contract is exercised once under OpenCode. This PR's behavior is almost entirely declarative frontmatter and prompt wiring, so a single smoke run provides much more confidence than static review alone.
